body:
<!-- Beschrijf wat deze pull request doet. Voeg een samenvatting van de wijzigingen en de reden voor de wijzigingen toe. -->
Deze pull request implementeert alle *class* functionaliteit omtrent het beheer en overzicht.

Er wordt een pagina toegevoegd waarop een leerling een overzicht kan zien van alle klassen waar hij deel van is. Bij klikken op het aantal leden, krijgt hij een overzicht met alle klasgenoten van die klas. Verder is er een veld voorzien waarin de leerling een code kan ingeven om een klas te *joinen*. Deze geeft aan als het gebruikte formaat correct was of niet.

Er wordt een pagina toegevoegd waarop een leerkracht alle klassen waarvan hij beheerder is kan zien. Via deze pagina kan naar een pagina gegaan worden waar één klas beheerd kan worden (zie volgende paragraaf). Verder kan op deze pagina aan nieuwe klas gecreëerd worden door een displaynaam in te geven. Ook uitnodigingen van andere leerkrachten om een klas mee te beheren worden opgelijst met de mogelijkheid deze te accepteren of weigeren.

Als laatste werd een pagina toegevoegd waarop een leerkracht zijn klas kan beheren. Er wordt een lijst van studenten getoond met de mogelijkheid ze te verwijderen. Ook worden alle join requests opgelijst met de mogelijkheid deze te accepteren of verwijderen. Als laatste is er de mogelijkheid een andere leerkracht uit te nodigen.

author: jlucovsky
body:
Continuation of #13041  

Transforms that support optional strings, like from_base64 and pcrexform, should also support identity-data to treat transforms with like transform options as the same.

This commit demonstrates
- When computing a hash, include identity data from the transform
- When comparing, include the identity data from the transforms
- Omitting the "options" ptr from the transform hash/compare
- Modify xor, pcrexform, and from_base64 to supply identity data for disambiguation in the compare/hash logic.

Updates:
- Modify identity function to support rust better; now uses pointer, nbytes instead of a structure
- Update rust transforms with transform identity function
- Add identity to xor transform.
- Fix compiler warning when computing hash value for transforms (see https://github.com/OISF/suricata/pull/12971)
- Check memory allocation values
- Move identity data collection to hash table user (from hash computation function)
- Formatting fixup (again :-( )
- Rust clippy fixup
- Change term from "serialization" to "identity"
- Formatting fixup (see #13041 )

Idea:
Construct a binary tree in which each node represents some subset of the users and keeps track of total number of tickets of that subset of users.
The root node represent the whole set of users, and the children of a node are _partition_ of that node, i.e. they are disjoint set of users but together the union is the node.
To distribute a prize, start from root, and trigger the random number generator upon each node, based on the relative number of tickets.

Space complexity:
$O(U)$, where $U$ is number  of users, a major improvement from $O(T)$ where $T$ being total number of tickets in the generic array of tickets implementation.

Time complexity:
Assuming constant time random number generation, $O((P+U) \times \lg{U})$: the tree being initialized to a complete binary tree, each time a user/ticket is chosen takes $O(h = \lg{U})$ time.
If the user turns out invalid, number of users is decreased by $1$.
If the user is valid, number of prizes is decreased by $1$.
Thus at most we trigger the tree traversal $O((P+U) \times \lg{U})$ times. Again, if assuming random number generation is constant time, the time complexity thus follows.

body:
This pull request introduces a set of changes to implement authentication and user management features in the Angular application. Key updates include the addition of interceptors for handling API requests, services for managing authentication and the current user, and configuration changes to support environment-specific settings.

### Authentication and User Management:

* **Authentication Service**: Added `AuthService` to handle login, token refresh, and logout operations using API endpoints. It includes methods for managing the access token. (`src/app/features/auth/services/auth.service.ts`, [src/app/features/auth/services/auth.service.tsR1-R46](diffhunk://#diff-096baf431727c98c57564615643faacad9b3c147478ae0aa59d1165b9281ab94R1-R46))
* **Current User Service**: Added `CurrentUserService` to manage the currently logged-in user, including loading the user data on app initialization and providing a reactive user state. (`src/app/core/services/current-user.service.ts`, [src/app/core/services/current-user.service.tsR1-R38](diffhunk://#diff-02e691ac4e0b7e762b76969176f77acdc07c5ff15704727df5d567faee4fa08fR1-R38))

### HTTP Interceptors:

* **Base URL Interceptor**: Added `baseUrlInterceptor` to prepend the base API URL to relative HTTP requests. (`src/app/core/interceptors/base-url.interceptor.ts`, [src/app/core/interceptors/base-url.interceptor.tsR1-R17](diffhunk://#diff-6779767a58d74bcfaa45863e4b7ba80148abb5f4dc0902fee9627ea08efc809eR1-R17))
* **Authentication Interceptor**: Added `authInterceptor` to attach the authorization token to outgoing requests and handle token refresh on `401 Unauthorized` responses. (`src/app/features/auth/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts`, [src/app/features/auth/interceptors/auth.interceptor.tsR1-R48](diffhunk://#diff-5ed23efde7d3e25c763bf6e8f8ca5697a8547e399cffe02734b76981048374c9R1-R48))

### Configuration and Environment Setup:

* **Environment Configuration**: Added `environment` and `environment.development` files to manage environment-specific settings, such as the API base URL. (`src/environments/environment.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d897f7d114ca657c43905bff9a6ee17e53e2d1ccc172b7c258a54183653a691aR1-R4); `src/environments/environment.development.ts`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a8781811a71ccc5e6e8919aa7054cf3a9c66d8624b4687cb9029aa12a5b93049R1-R3)

### API Models and Constants:

* **API Endpoints**: Added `API_ENDPOINTS` constant to centralize API endpoint definitions. (`src/app/core/constants/api-endpoints.constants.ts`, [src/app/core/constants/api-endpoints.constants.tsR1-R8](diffhunk://#diff-bd28b64b161ddd6f05e4206d569b94d20ea9b078aba0c5764923fc12d30a00daR1-R8))
* **DTO Models**: Added data transfer object (DTO) models for login requests, login responses, and token refresh responses. (`src/app/features/auth/models/login-request.dto.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1d34578878a3a43dbb7a2d85d9dce5c3e2b629371383514df506cce9bb44ac81R1-R6); `src/app/features/auth/models/login-response.dto.ts`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d28eb271251590d0b86965a97c52af9a6cfdd9a23c17ddbb8b343ec95b9085a5R1-R3); `src/app/features/auth/models/refresh-token-response.dto.ts`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d85d137dd88b4ab59b2c4df07593b14be41d64d970443750c7b9a2ba8f947157R1-R4)

### Testing:

* **Unit Tests**: Added basic unit tests for `AuthService` and `CurrentUserService` to ensure their creation and initialization. When an invite link is deleted by a developer, the page returned is a generic 404 page. This pr add additional logic to handle the 404 response with a new `"deleted"` status.

author: dlek-user
body:
# [62] Unique Paths

## 문제 설명 

There is a robot on an `m x n` grid. The robot is initially located at the **top-left corner** (i.e., `grid[0][0]`). The robot tries to move to the **bottom-right corner** (i.e., `grid[m - 1][n - 1]`). The robot can only move either down or right at any point in time.

Given the two integers `m` and `n`, return _the number of possible unique paths that the robot can take to reach the bottom-right corner_.

The test cases are generated so that the answer will be less than or equal to `2 * 109`.

 

#### Example 1:


> Input: m = 3, n = 7
> Output: 28

#### Example 2:

> Input: m = 3, n = 2
> Output: 3
> Explanation: From the top-left corner, there are a total of 3 ways to reach the bottom-right corner:
> 1. Right -> Down -> Down
> 2. Down -> Down -> Right
> 3. Down -> Right -> Down

## 코드 설명

```
class Solution {
    public int uniquePaths(int m, int n) {
        long result = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= m - 1; i++) {
            result = result * (n - 1 + i) / i;
        }
        return (int) result;
    }
}
```
#
```
long result = 1;
```
결과 값을 저장할 변수입니다.
중간 계산에서 오버플로우를 방지하기 위해 long 타입 사용





```
for (int i = 1; i <= m - 1; i++)
```
조합 수식을 계산하기 위한 반복문입니다.
우리는 (m + n - 2)C(m - 1)을 계산하려고 하므로, 분자에서 n - 1 + i를 곱하고, 분모에서 i로 나눕니다.






```
result = result * (n - 1 + i) / i;
```
이 줄은 조합 수 C(m+n-2, m-1)을 누적 곱셈과 나눗셈으로 계산하는 부분입니다.






```
return (int) result;
```
정답은 10억 이하라고 명시되어 있으므로, int로 변환해서 반환해도 안전합니다.

author: hslim001
body:
문제 난이도 : 골드 4
문제 유형 : 시뮬레이션 , 큐

[뱀](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/3190)

## 문제 코드
```python
## 시간복잡도 : 64ms
## 공간복잡도 : 35004kb
from collections import deque

length = int(input())
apple_num = int(input())
arr = [[0] * length for _ in range(length)]
arr[0][0] = 1
que = deque([(0, 0)])
for _ in range(apple_num):
    y, x = map(int, input().split())
    arr[y - 1][x - 1] = 2
command_num = int(input())
command = []
for _ in range(command_num):
    time, d = input().split()
    if d == 'L':
        command.append((int(time), 0))
    else:
        command.append((int(time), 1))
direc = 1
rotate = [(3, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (2, 0)]
dy = [-1, 0, 1, 0]
dx = [0, 1, 0, -1]
y, x = 0, 0
time = 0
pointer = 0
while 1:
    time += 1
    y += dy[direc]
    x += dx[direc]
    if not(0 <= y < length and 0 <= x < length) or arr[y][x] == 1:
        break   # 벽과 몸에 부딫히면 종료
    que.append((y, x))
    if arr[y][x] != 2:
        tempy, tempx = que.popleft()
        arr[tempy][tempx] = 0
    arr[y][x] = 1

    if pointer < command_num and time == command[pointer][0]:
        direc = rotate[direc][command[pointer][1]]
        pointer += 1
print(time)
```

## 풀이 방식
- 이동 방향으로 한칸 전진, 벽이나 자신의 몸을 만나면 끝.
- 만약 사과가 그 칸에 있으면, 전진 후 다음 사이클
- 만약 빈 칸이면, 큐에서 꼬리를 팝 시키고 그 칸을 빈칸으로 만들어줌.
- 커맨드 명령 시간이 된다면, 그 명령대로 방향 전환. 
- 반복

author: jamiras
body:
Maintains a running **playtime** metric on each `player_games` record, and fully recalculates it, as well and **time to beat** and **time to master** metrics any time an achievement is unlocked. These are further aggregated into median metrics on the `GameData` table, which can be shown on the individual game pages:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b21994-dba7-42af-b556-fb7a25587f48)
The small number in parenthesis is the number of data points used to find the median.

This value is calculated for each player using the actual sessions tracked in the database starting with the datetime of the first published achievement. Times prior to Oct 2023 (when we started tracking sessions) are estimated from achievement unlocks, but are still included in the metrics. It is hoped that the estimated values are statistically similar to real values and/or will be diminished by having more real values than estimated ones. 

We may wish to only aggregate values newer than Oct 2023 when calculating the median metrics on the `GameData` table to eliminate the estimated values. We could also consider only aggregating the last year's worth of data to minimize the impact of revisions.

For many games, the softcore times don't differ that much from the hardcore times. I'm wondering if we want to just show the hardcore times and maybe eliminate the softcore times or move them to a tooltip?

Future PRs will use this data for the recently played games list and annual recap command. It could probably also be displayed in the player progress widget on the game page.

-----

To recalculate the metrics for a single game:
```
sail artisan ra:platform:game:update-player-games [gameid]
```

To recalculate all metrics (warning: this took around 40 hours on my VM to process all 18M records):
```
sail artisan ra:platform:player:update-estimated-times
sail artisan ra:platform:game:update-metrics
```
-----

For prod, I plan to just let this run naturally for a couple months to fill any `player_games` being actively played. Then, add a scheduled action that processes a handful of records every few minutes. If the count of unprocessed backfill is low enough (unlikely), then we could just use the commands.

Since data is going to be sparse (at least initially), the changes to the mastery widget are only displayed in local environments.

author: shuakami
body:
This PR improves the reminder check mechanism to handle various edge cases and potential issues:

### Improvements
- Added absolute time-based checking instead of relative intervals
- Implemented proper handling of time drift and processing delays
- Added compensation for missed reminders due to system pauses or delays
- Enhanced error handling and recovery

### Technical Details
1. Time Management:
   - Uses absolute timestamps for checking instead of fixed intervals
   - Calculates precise wait times to next minute boundary
   - Maintains last check time to ensure no reminders are missed

2. Error Handling:
   - Individual reminder failures don't affect other reminders
   - Main loop errors trigger quick recovery with time compensation
   - Added 65-second lookback on error recovery to prevent missing reminders

3. Performance:
   - Batch processing of due reminders
   - Reduced file I/O operations
   - Minimum sleep time to prevent CPU thrashing

### Testing
The improved mechanism has been tested for:
- Long processing time scenarios
- System time adjustments
- Program pause/resume situations
- Error recovery and reminder compensation

This fix ensures more reliable reminder delivery even in edge cases where processing time exceeds the check interval or when system time changes occur.

## 🌱WIL
- 이번 스터디 발제 문제를 풀면서 백트래킹 유형이 처음이라는 것을 알게 되었다. 발제 문제 풀이를 들으면서까지는 정확히 어떤 느낌인지 잘 와닿지는 않았는데 조건 있는 완전탐색이라고 보면 되는 건가 라는 느낌으로 이해했다. 종료조건을 꼭 정의하고, 선택하지 않은 경우의 수를 탐색하고, 선택을 계속 반영해주는 것이 특징인 것 같다. 다른 기본 문제들을 같이 풀어봐야겠다. 
  ```python
  def backtrack(상태):
      if 종료조건(상태):
          정답 처리
          return
  
      for 선택 in 가능한 선택들:
          if 유효하지 않은 선택:
              continue
  
          상태에 선택 추가
          backtrack(업데이트된 상태)
          선택 되돌리기 (상태 복구)
  ```
- 매주 한 주제씩은 개념+기본문제+발제/과제 난이도 문제를 정리하면서 가고 싶은데 매번 작심N일이다(근데 이제 N이 3이하일때...). 다음주는 백트래킹이나 DP 문제 유형을 풀어보고싶다! 실버 문제들을 많이 풀어보고 힌트 없이 쓱쓱 풀어낼 수 있게 만들고 싶다. 일단 꾸준히 하기 🫠

## 🚀주간 목표 문제 수: 3개
> 푼 문제
- [백준 #1759. 암호 만들기](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1759): 그래프 / 골드5
- [백준 #6603. 로또](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/6603): 그래프 / 실버2
- [백준 #15649. N과 M (1)](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/15649): 그래프 / 실버3

---
## [백준 #1759. 암호 만들기](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1759): 백트래킹 / 골드5
### 🚩제출한 코드
```python
import sys 
input = sys.stdin.readline
from itertools import combinations

L, C = map(int, input().split())
chars = input().split()
chars.sort() # 오름차순 정렬 

vowels = set('aeiou')
result = []

# 백트래킹: 해를 찾는 도중 해가 아니어서 막히면, 되돌아가서 다시 해를 찾아가는 기법
# 현재까지 만든 암호의 길이가 L이면 종료 조건 
# 모음/자음 개수를 체크해서 만족할 경우 출력 
# 그렇지 않으면 다음 알파벳을 선택해 재귀 호출 
def backtrack(path, start):
    # 1. 종료 조건: 길이가 L이면 조합 완성 
    if len(path) == L: 
        vowel_count = 0 
        consonant_count = 0 
        
        # 모음/자음 개수 세기 
        for ch in path: 
            if ch in vowels: 
                vowel_count += 1
            else: 
                consonant_count += 1 
        
        # 조건에 맞으면 출력 
        if vowel_count >= 1 and consonant_count >= 2: 
            print(''.join(path))
        return 
    
    # 2. 가능한 모든 문자에 대해 선택
    for i in range(start, C): # C == len(chars)
        # 선택 
        path.append(chars[i])
        # 재귀 호출(다음 문자 선택) - 조합이므로 i+1부터
        backtrack(path, i+1)
        # 선택 취소  
        path.pop()
        
# 탐색 시작 
backtrack([], 0)
```

## [백준 #6603. 로또](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/6603): 백트래킹 / 실버2
### 🚩제출한 코드
```python
import sys

def backtrack(S, path, start):
    if len(path) == 6:
        print(' '.join(map(str, path)))
        return
    for i in range(start, len(S)):
        path.append(S[i])
        backtrack(S, path, i + 1)
        path.pop()

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
first_case = True

for line in lines:
    if line == '0':
        break

    parts = list(map(int, line.strip().split()))
    S = parts[1:]

    if not first_case:
        print()
    first_case = False

    backtrack(S, [], 0)
```

## [백준 #15649. N과 M (1)](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/15649): 백트래킹 / 실버3
### 🚩제출한 코드
```python
N, M = map(int, input().split())
visited = [False] * (N + 1)  # 1부터 N까지 사용 여부
result = []

def backtrack():
    if len(result) == M:
        print(' '.join(map(str, result)))
        return
    
    for i in range(1, N + 1):
        if not visited[i]:
            visited[i] = True
            result.append(i)
            backtrack()
            result.pop()         # 상태 복원
            visited[i] = False   # 방문 초기화

backtrack()
```

body:
## 🍀 작업 사항

### 1️⃣  점주 주문 갱신 이벤트 모델링

```java
public record StoreOrderEvent(
	Long tableId,
	Integer tableNumber,
	Order order
) {
	public record Order(
		Long orderId,
		LocalDateTime createdAt,
		List<OrderMenu> orderMenu
	) {
		public record OrderMenu(
			Long menuId,
			String menuName,
			Integer menuPrice,
			Integer menuCount,
			String menuStatus // TODO : 추후 enum으로 변경
		) {
		}
	}
}
``` 

- 점주는 위 데이터에 해당하는 정보를 실시간으로 SSE 서버로부터 받습니다.


### 2️⃣ SSE subscribe 개발

- 클라이언트와 SSE 서버간에 데이터 통신시 다음과 같은 신뢰성 없는 통신이 생길 수 있습니다. 
1. 데이터 유실
2. 데이터 중복
3. 데이터 순서 꼬임

- 데이터 중복은 이벤트 데이터 안에 orderId라는 Order 일련번호가 있기 때문에 중복 처리는 클라이언트에서 처리 가능하다고 판단
- 데이터 순서 꼬임은 유실만 되지 않는다면 문제 없다고 판단

마지막 데이터 유실은 다음 상황에서 발생할 수 있습니다

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/981ae7dd-a497-473e-b6b6-21896774b329)

따라서 다음과 같이 클라이언트가 재연결시 fetch 하는 rest api 를 제공하여 이를 해소할 수 있습니다

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fe34d76-504c-4540-9358-31a225ba4098)

하지만 fetch 를 한다고 해도 다음과 같은 상황에서 데이터 유실을 탐지할 수 없습니다.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a607d4a-e256-486c-aaea-ef5bf0421232)

결론은 SSE 커넥션 타임아웃을 짧게 가져가서 데이터가 유실되더라도 최대한 빠르게 이를 알아챌 수 있도록 했습니다.


## ❓ 의논 사항

- 추가로 점주가 테이블의 활성화 내역(몇번 테이블 활성화되어 있는지 같은)을 실시간으로 새로고침 하지 않고 받을지 고민해야 함 ( 필요하다면 StoreOrderEvent 와 별개의 이벤트를 모델링할 예정)
- 사용자가 동시 주문시 장바구니에 담을 때 실시간으로 내역을 받을 필요 있다면 이벤트를 추가할 예정

author: justinwilaby
body:
# PR: Optimize Tool and Schema Descriptions 
[W-18327057](https://gus.lightning.force.com/a07EE00002DBFllYAH)
This PR reduces token counts and improves accuracy for tool choice and use by the LLM. Observed behavior shows a stark improvement across the board versus the previous implementation.

## Changes
- Streamlined tool descriptions across 11 files to reduce token count while maintaining clarity
- Simplified schema descriptions for Heroku tools (apps, addons, maintenance, pipelines, etc.)
- Removed redundant documentation while preserving essential information
- Consolidated parameter descriptions to be more concise
- Removed `--json` flag from `list_apps`

## Impact
- Reduced overall token count by removing 644 lines while adding 188 lines of optimized content
- Maintained functionality while improving documentation efficiency
- Better resource utilization in tool descriptions

## Business Value
- Reduces API response payload sizes, leading to faster API interactions
- Improves developer experience since LLMs can better reason about which tools to use

## Testing Instructions
### Verify tool functionality:
1. Use prompts to trigger tool usage for each tool.
2. Use prompts to trigger complex workflows requiring the use of multiple tools

## Notes
- No functional changes - purely description optimizations
- All existing tool behaviors remain unchanged

author: magtheo
body:
This PR significantly improves the terrain system by implementing multi-threaded chunk processing, binary storage format, and optimized biome blending. These changes enhance performance, reduce memory usage, and provide a more consistent visual experience.
Key Changes
Performance Improvements

Binary Storage Format: Replaced JSON with binary serialization for chunk data, dramatically reducing file sizes and I/O overhead
Multi-threaded Chunk Generation: Offloaded mesh generation to worker threads, improving framerate during terrain generation
Spatial Grid for Biome Lookup: Implemented a ThreadSafeBiomeData with spatial grid for faster biome queries
LRU Cache: Updated ChunkStorage to use a more efficient LRU caching system

Configuration System Refactor

Lazy-loaded Global Configuration: Introduced TOML-based global configuration with lazy loading
Thread-safe Config Access: Implemented RwLock pattern for safe multi-threaded access to configuration
Streamlined Initialization: Adapted SystemInitializer to work with the new configuration system

Visual Improvements

Correct Triangle Winding Order: Fixed vertex winding order for proper face culling
Per-vertex Normal Calculation: Implemented finite difference method for smoother terrain normals
Consistent Biome Blending: Enhanced biome transitions by implementing a consistent blending algorithm in worker threads

Code Quality

Removed Unused Code: Cleaned up bridges and other unused components
Updated Noise Path: Improved noise generation with new implementation path
Export Preset: Added standardized export configuration

Technical Details

The ChunkStorage system now handles Godot Vector2/Vector3 serialization with custom wrappers that implement Serde traits
Worker threads safely communicate with the main thread via channels and thread-safe data structures
Terrain mesh generation now happens off the main thread, allowing for smoother gameplay during world generation
Configuration is now centralized and accessible throughout the codebase with proper thread safety

Thank you for submitting this pull request. We really appreciate you spending the time to work on SurrealDB. 🚀 🎉 

## What is the motivation?

<!-- Please provide details on the motivation for why you have made this change.-->

In #5805 I added new lints at the workspace level. While making another change I noticed that they were not actually being applied to the sub-crates in the repo.

## What does this change do?

<!-- Please provide a description of what this pull request does, and how it solves the problem. -->

This change applies the lints to the whole workspace including sub-crates and fixes all of the linting issues that were found as a result.

Approach / changes:
1. I fixed all of the lints in the first change.
2. For the `unused_async` change, I took the following approach:
    1. ~Any `new` functions that did not use async I converted to be non-async.~
    2. ~For a few targeted async functions which were very small, I changed them to be non-async.~
    3. ~For all others, I just added the `#[expect(clippy::unused_async)]` attribute. I did this to avoid making too many changes which may affect where we're yielding in the compute path.~
    4. ~If, as you're reviewing this, you think that some functions should have been left as async even though they were not using any async functionality, just leave a comment and I'll revert those changes.~
    5. I ended up reverting all of this because the release build was stack overflowing with these changes. Making them async again fixed the issue.
3. I replaced all `allow` attributes and replaced them with `expect` and then fixed or removed any that were not actually firing.
4. I fixed the `kv_fdb` rust configuration to be a feature named `kv-fdb` like all of the other features. This was found due to the correct inheritance of the workspace lints to the sub-crates.

## What is your testing strategy?

<!-- Write your test plan here. Please provide us with clear instructions on how you verified your changes work. -->

Automated CI testing should be sufficient.

body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description

This PR allow us to use CSS gradients (linear or radial) in color swatches, which we actually had a use-case for in the an Umbraco 13 project, but due a limitation in the approved color picker, we made a "hack" to solves this.
https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco.UI/discussions/1018

The color should be a valid CSS background (including linear/radial gradient), but the value could possible any string value with e.g. `gradient` or something else from a hex color.

Of course the core approved colors in CMS can still validate a hex color, but this change allow us to use gradient in a custom property editor.

Some CSS gradient examples:
https://uigradients.com/
https://cssgradient.io/
https://webgradients.com/
https://coolors.co/gradients

## Types of changes

<!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Chore (minor updates related to the tooling or maintenance of the repository, does not impact compiled assets)

## Motivation and context

It allow us to use CSS background colors as well and not only solid colors.
This could be useful in custom implementations in property editors, dashboards etc. and using specific frontend features like e.g. Tailwind CSS gradients:
https://tailscan.com/gradients

Furthermore some inspiration from Fluent UI library here:
https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/components-swatchpicker--docs&globals=storybook_fluentui-react-addon_theme:web-light#color-swatch-variants

author: fielding
body:
**Description**  
This PR addresses a deprecation warning in Diffusers 0.33.0 related to the `output_type` parameter in `get_2d_sincos_pos_embed`. The function now recommends using `output_type='pt'` to return a PyTorch tensor directly, which is more efficient and avoids unnecessary conversions from NumPy.

**Changes**  
- Modified `get_2d_sincos_pos_embed` in `xfuser/model_executor/layers/embeddings.py` to use `output_type='pt'`.  
- Added the `device` parameter to ensure the tensor is placed directly on the correct device, removing the need for manual device transfer.  
- Removed the previous `torch.from_numpy` conversion and `.to(latent.device)` call, as they are no longer required these changes.

**Benefits**  
- Ensures xFuser remains compatible with Diffusers' updated API, avoiding future issues.  
- Improves performance by eliminating NumPy-to-PyTorch conversions and redundant device transfers.  
- Simplifies the code.

**Testing**  
- Tested with Diffusers 0.33.0.dev0 live on a 8x H200 machine. Can report back testings on a more variety of machines if needed.

Cheers

body:
This pull request includes extensive updates to the Yukino documentation, focusing on improving clarity, adding missing details, and updating code examples to reflect recent API changes. Key changes include restructuring event handling in the `voice-state` guide, expanding the `connectors` and `rest` API documentation, introducing new sections for `Player` and `Queue` APIs, and updating imports to use `yukinojs` instead of `yukino`. Below is a breakdown of the most important changes:

### Voice State Management Updates
* Replaced the `voiceDisconnected` event with `wsClosed` for better handling of WebSocket closure scenarios and added more descriptive logging and reconnection logic.
* Updated the auto-disconnect example to provide clearer implementation guidance.
* Clarified monitoring connection state using the `debug` event.

### Connector API Enhancements
* Added detailed constructor requirements for the `Connector` class, including mandatory and optional parameters.
* Enhanced the `createNode` method to accept optional REST options and clarified that `destroyNode` and `destroyPlayer` are not implemented in the base class. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-18fba328b6646fa9aab3a2588a195311f6694d904979c87f4fdf70e9ebc10106L23-R32) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-18fba328b6646fa9aab3a2588a195311f6694d904979c87f4fdf70e9ebc10106L34-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-18fba328b6646fa9aab3a2588a195311f6694d904979c87f4fdf70e9ebc10106L49-R96)
* Updated voice state management to emphasize internal handling via the `raw` event in `DiscordJSConnector`.

### REST API Improvements
* Expanded the `loadTracks` method to support specifying a search source and added new methods like `destroyAllPlayers` and `updateVoiceServer`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3eee189a3d18a8b5513a75164767c223b7f6020f43288ecaa57f422376c3d18aL22-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3eee189a3d18a8b5513a75164767c223b7f6020f43288ecaa57f422376c3d18aR113-R133)
* Introduced generic HTTP methods (`get`, `post`, `patch`, `delete`, `request`) for advanced use cases.

### Player and Queue Documentation
* Added a comprehensive new section detailing the `Player` and `Queue` APIs, including playback control, track management, filters, voice connection, and queue manipulation methods.

### General Documentation Updates
* Standardized imports across all files to use `yukinojs` instead of `yukino`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e9ff2a5318c3bccca2e7f3753b4e29c1cba76784e8ae033b936ec29e578bbb7dL16-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3eee189a3d18a8b5513a75164767c223b7f6020f43288ecaa57f422376c3d18aL3-R8)
* Expanded the `Types` reference to include detailed descriptions of constants like `Events`, `LoadTypes`, `State`, and `PlayerStates`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8d60076a4155c3b4cf0e3235ba868e9c6a39aa7251ae68a8af0ab5459cd686caR3-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8d60076a4155c3b4cf0e3235ba868e9c6a39aa7251ae68a8af0ab5459cd686caR22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8d60076a4155c3b4cf0e3235ba868e9c6a39aa7251ae68a8af0ab5459cd686caL36-R51)

   ### 23.2

   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Document calendar-based versioning scheme (:issue:`716`)
* Enforce that the entire marker string is parsed (:issue:`687`)

* Canonicalize names for requirements comparison (:issue:`644`)

* Correctly handle non-normalised specifiers in requirements (:issue:`634`)

body:
This pull request refactors and improves the blog functionality by consolidating JavaScript logic, removing inline scripts, and enhancing maintainability. Key changes include replacing inline event handlers with `data-action` attributes, migrating JavaScript logic to external files, and simplifying the structure of the blog's HTML and CSS.

### JavaScript Refactoring and Consolidation:

* Consolidated JavaScript functionality into `js/blog.js`, including handling actions like post deletion, comment toggling, and navigation. Removed redundant logic from `scripts/blog_interactions.js` and deleted the file. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3d6ebcd79ff3f9cdb402dd7c319bf67c6b5e4c4bf10f2b2e502b27c07df63c64R1-R117)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f277e7a6e8deae04f17767d8a23808d21b172d66a641fb66a759ed87a8d17277L1-L94)`)
* Moved preview functionality to a new file `scripts/preview.js` and success popup logic to `scripts/successPopup.js`, cleaning up inline scripts in `create_blog.php`. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-45a60045fb271e11e3d3d1dafe3f69ea1861c2944a682eb9a2579a3518d05a8fR1-R26)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-94dede53a6ef48dbf40d53866835309a429acc738ded4d15dcea10220d0fa260R1-R3)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1d418eec23ef38e96b5acfc0de8e391a599d90daca5415eea6d58268d55a0e44L145-R147)`)

### HTML Updates for Event Handling:

* Replaced inline JavaScript event handlers with `data-action` attributes for buttons across multiple pages (e.g., delete post, delete comment, back to editor). (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d88a459c47b2d238fe9b088ed399024b6a113cf75053375406840212a9c7afb3L276-R276)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1d418eec23ef38e96b5acfc0de8e391a599d90daca5415eea6d58268d55a0e44L127-R127)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1f5efc44809ec7394c1716cc355cccff63757333d680401df539a099d8c32c41L218-L233)`)
* Removed unnecessary modal-related elements and logic for comment handling, simplifying the HTML structure in `viewBlog.php`. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1f5efc44809ec7394c1716cc355cccff63757333d680401df539a099d8c32c41L256-L281)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f5efc44809ec7394c1716cc355cccff63757333d680401df539a099d8c32c41L291-R274)`)

### CSS and Structural Improvements:

* Updated the comment modal's CSS to improve clarity and maintainability by explicitly defining visibility states. (`[styles/blog_enhanced.cssL206-R219](diffhunk://#diff-04f0889b3d81403edefaaf087cbc224aa94856c8b5bd7a55405f50a0531412fbL206-R219)`)
* Streamlined the inclusion of JavaScript files across pages, ensuring consistent behavior by adding `js/blog.js` and `js/mobile-menu.js` where necessary. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-22b81f5225af557ef5fe3f7b2c2f2fc39f19786f5e167da8b9085f5b60f5e71cR43-R44)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f5efc44809ec7394c1716cc355cccff63757333d680401df539a099d8c32c41L310-R293)`)

These changes improve code readability, maintainability, and scalability by centralizing JavaScript logic, reducing redundancy, and adhering to best practices for event handling and modularization.

author: deshan-samarathunga
body:
…improvements

Auto Logout System

Introduced SessionManager.jsx and activityMonitor.js to handle user inactivity and trigger logout after 30 minutes.

Used window.dispatchEvent(new Event("activity")) within axios interceptor to reset the timer on every request.

JWT Refresh Token Integration

Backend: AuthController.java updated to issue and refresh access tokens using secure cookies.

Added JWT utility improvements in JwtUtil.java, with configurable token durations.

Frontend: Axios interceptor (axiosInstance.js) now handles silent token refresh on 401 errors.

Post Deletion UX Revamp

Enhanced DeleteModal.jsx with proper visibility in dark theme.

Improved layout and button styles for clarity.

Community Page Readability Fix

Updated CommunityPage.jsx to ensure better font contrast in dark mode.

Security Enhancements

Implemented token expiry check using jwtDecode.

Removed expired tokens from localStorage on page load or decode failure.

UI Tweaks & Fixes

Toast notification appears 1 minute before session expiration.

Sidebar and Topbar refactored for better interaction handling and session awareness.

author: nickersoft
body:
This PR adds support for word forms, as well as lemmas on Entry objects:

```xml
<entry term="jumping" lemma="jump"></entry>
```

```xml
<entry term="jump">
<forms>
<form>jumping</form>
<form>jumper</form>
<form>
```

as well as a new EntryRef type for referencing entries in the same dictionary, as well as FormKind enum to support a "kind" attribute on the `<form>` nodes.

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

This PR implements asset loading optimization for the MainWP Child plugin to improve performance in the WordPress admin area. The changes include:

1. Creating a dedicated MainWP_Child_Assets class to handle asset loading
2. Implementing conditional loading of CSS and JavaScript files only on MainWP-specific pages
3. Separating asset registration from enqueuing for better performance
4. Refactoring the MainWP_Clone_Page class to use the centralized asset loading system
5. Optimizing jQuery UI loading to only load when needed

These changes significantly reduce the plugin's impact on admin page load times by preventing unnecessary CSS and JavaScript files from being loaded on non-MainWP pages.

### How to test the changes in this Pull Request:

1. Install the MainWP Child plugin on a WordPress site
2. Navigate through various admin pages and note the scripts and styles loaded before applying the changes (using browser dev tools)
3. Apply the changes and navigate through the same pages - you should see fewer scripts and styles loaded on non-MainWP pages
4. Verify that all MainWP Child functionality still works correctly on MainWP-specific pages
5. Check that the clone page still has all the necessary jQuery UI components loaded

author: devarajabc
body:
Remove the separate `mmapmem` red-black tree and merges its into `mapallmem`, reducing overall memory usage.

To distinguish memory regions that were previously tracked separately in `mmapmem`,
we now use a `mem_flag_t` bitmask enum in the data field of `mapallmem`:
```
    MEM_ALLOCATED = 1   // allocated
    MEM_RESERVED  = 2   // reserved 
    MEM_MMAP      = 3   // allocated via mmap()
```

In tests with `chess.exe` (Box64 + Wine), this reduced the total node count by ~81, saving ~4.4 KB of memory. 
The impact is expected to be greater in mmap-heavy programs.

Resolves #2546

**EDIT:** The total node count was reduced by approximately 189 nodes (the entire `mmapmem` tree).
It's not 81 as I previously mentioned.

This PR updates [packaging](https://pypi.org/project/packaging) from **20.8** to **25.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 25.0
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* PEP 751: Add support for ``extras`` and ``dependency_groups`` markers. (:issue:`885`)
* PEP 738: Add support for Android platform tags. (:issue:`880`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 24.2
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* PEP 639: Implement License-Expression and License-File (:issue:`828`)
* Use ``!r`` formatter for error messages with filenames (:issue:`844`)
* Add support for PEP 730 iOS tags (:issue:`832`)
* Fix prerelease detection for ``>`` and ``<`` (:issue:`794`)
* Fix uninformative error message (:issue:`830`)
* Refactor ``canonicalize_version`` (:issue:`793`)
* Patch python_full_version unconditionally (:issue:`825`)
* Fix doc for ``canonicalize_version`` to mention ``strip_trailing_zero`` and a typo in a docstring (:issue:`801`)
* Fix typo in Version ``__str__`` (:issue:`817`)
* Support creating a ``SpecifierSet`` from an iterable of ``Specifier`` objects (:issue:`775`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 24.1
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Document ``markers.default_environment()`` (:issue:`753`).
* Add support for Python 3.13 (:issue:`783`).
* Modernise type annotations (:issue:`785`).
* Work around ``platform.python_version()`` returning non PEP 440 compliant version
  for non-tagged CPython builds (:issue:`802`).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 24.0
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Do specifier matching correctly when the specifier contains an epoch number
  and has more components than the version (:issue:`683`)
* Support the experimental ``--disable-gil`` builds in packaging.tags
  (:issue:`727`)
* BREAKING: Make optional ``metadata.Metadata`` attributes default to ``None`` (:issue:`733`)
* Fix errors when trying to access the ``description_content_type``, ``keywords``,
  and ``requires_python`` attributes on ``metadata.Metadata`` when those values
  have not been provided (:issue:`733`)
* Fix a bug preventing the use of the built in ``ExceptionGroup`` on versions of
  Python that support it (:issue:`725`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 23.2
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Document calendar-based versioning scheme (:issue:`716`)
* Enforce that the entire marker string is parsed (:issue:`687`)
* Requirement parsing no longer automatically validates the URL (:issue:`120`)
* Canonicalize names for requirements comparison (:issue:`644`)
* Introduce ``metadata.Metadata`` (along with ``metadata.ExceptionGroup`` and ``metadata.InvalidMetadata``; :issue:`570`)
* Introduce the ``validate`` keyword parameter to ``utils.normalize_name()`` (:issue:`570`)
* Introduce ``utils.is_normalized_name()`` (:issue:`570`)
* Make ``utils.parse_sdist_filename()`` and ``utils.parse_wheel_filename()``
  raise ``InvalidSdistFilename`` and ``InvalidWheelFilename``, respectively,
  when the version component of the name is invalid
* Remove support for Python 3.7 (:issue:`783`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 23.1
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Parse raw metadata (:issue:`671`)
* Import underlying parser functions as an underscored variable (:issue:`663`)
* Improve error for local version label with unsupported operators (:issue:`675`)
* Add dedicated error for specifiers with incorrect `.*` suffix
* Replace spaces in platform names with underscores (:issue:`620`)
* Relax typing of ``_key`` on ``_BaseVersion`` (:issue:`669`)
* Handle prefix match with zeros at end of prefix correctly (:issue:`674`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 23.0
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Allow ``"extra"`` to be ``None`` in the marker environment (:issue:`650`)
* Refactor ``tags._generic_api`` to use ``EXT_SUFFIX`` (:issue:`607`)
* Correctly handle trailing whitespace on URL requirements (:issue:`642`)
* Fix typing for ``specifiers.BaseSpecifier.filter()`` (:issue:`643`)
* Use stable Python 3.11 in tests (:issue:`641`)
* Correctly handle non-normalised specifiers in requirements (:issue:`634`)
* Move to ``src/`` layout (:issue:`626`)
* Remove ``__about__`` file, in favour of keeping constants in ``__init__`` (:issue:`626`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 22.0
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Explicitly declare support for Python 3.11 (:issue:`587`)
* Remove support for Python 3.6 (:issue:`500`)
* Remove ``LegacySpecifier`` and ``LegacyVersion`` (:issue:`407`)
* Add ``__hash__`` and ``__eq__`` to ``Requirement`` (:issue:`499`)
* Add a ``cpNNN-none-any`` tag (:issue:`541`)
* Adhere to :pep:`685` when evaluating markers with extras (:issue:`545`)
* Allow accepting locally installed prereleases with ``SpecifierSet``  (:issue:`515`)
* Allow pre-release versions in marker evaluation (:issue:`523`)
* Correctly parse ELF for musllinux on Big Endian (:issue:`538`)
* Document ``packaging.utils.NormalizedName`` (:issue:`565`)
* Document exceptions raised by functions in ``packaging.utils`` (:issue:`544`)
* Fix compatible version specifier incorrectly strip trailing ``0`` (:issue:`493`)
* Fix macOS platform tags with old macOS SDK (:issue:`513`)
* Forbid prefix version matching on pre-release/post-release segments (:issue:`563`)
* Normalize specifier version for prefix matching (:issue:`561`)
* Improve documentation for ``packaging.specifiers`` and ``packaging.version``. (:issue:`572`)
* ``Marker.evaluate`` will now assume evaluation environment with empty ``extra``.
  Evaluating markers like ``"extra == 'xyz'"`` without passing any extra in the
  ``environment`` will no longer raise an exception (:issue:`550`)
* Remove dependency on ``pyparsing``, by replacing it with a hand-written parser.
  This package now has no runtime dependencies (:issue:`468`)
* Update return type hint for ``Specifier.filter`` and ``SpecifierSet.filter``
  to use ``Iterator`` instead of ``Iterable`` (:issue:`584`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.3
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Add a ``pp3-none-any`` tag (:issue:`311`)
* Replace the blank pyparsing 3 exclusion with a 3.0.5 exclusion (:issue:`481`, :issue:`486`)
* Fix a spelling mistake (:issue:`479`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.2
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Update documentation entry for 21.1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.1
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Update pin to pyparsing to exclude 3.0.0.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* PEP 656: musllinux support (:issue:`411`)
* Drop support for Python 2.7, Python 3.4 and Python 3.5.
* Replace distutils usage with sysconfig (:issue:`396`)
* Add support for zip files in ``parse_sdist_filename`` (:issue:`429`)
* Use cached ``_hash`` attribute to short-circuit tag equality comparisons (:issue:`417`)
* Specify the default value for the ``specifier`` argument to ``SpecifierSet`` (:issue:`437`)
* Proper keyword-only "warn" argument in packaging.tags (:issue:`403`)
* Correctly remove prerelease suffixes from ~= check (:issue:`366`)
* Fix type hints for ``Version.post`` and ``Version.dev`` (:issue:`393`)
* Use typing alias ``UnparsedVersion`` (:issue:`398`)
* Improve type inference for ``packaging.specifiers.filter()`` (:issue:`430`)
* Tighten the return type of ``canonicalize_version()`` (:issue:`402`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 20.9
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Run `isort <https://pypi.org/project/isort/>`_ over the code base (:issue:`377`)
* Add support for the ``macosx_10_*_universal2`` platform tags (:issue:`379`)
* Introduce ``packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename()`` and ``parse_sdist_filename()``
  (:issue:`387` and :issue:`389`)
   ```
   
  
</details>


 

<details>

  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/packaging
  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/packaging/
</details>

author: agboolaephraim
body:
Summary
This PR introduces a complete AI-based intrusion detection system focused on detecting Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks using supervised machine learning techniques. The system leverages the UNSW-NB15 dataset, with preprocessed flow data used to train, test, and simulate real-time detection of MITM attack patterns.

 What's Included
train_model.py: Trains a Decision Tree Classifier using labeled network traffic data.

live_detection.py: Simulates real-time detection by loading the trained model and performing predictions on new input data.

scaler.pkl: Saved StandardScaler for consistent feature preprocessing.

model.pkl: Serialized trained model used for inference.

README.md: Documentation with project overview, theoretical background, setup guide, and usage instructions.

Dataset CSV files extracted from the UNSW-NB15 dataset (placed in local directory, not pushed due to size).

 Theoretical Background & Concepts Covered
This project demonstrates a solid understanding of the following cybersecurity and AI-related principles:

MITM Attack Techniques: ARP Spoofing, DNS Hijacking, SSL Stripping.

Network Traffic Analysis: Flow-based feature extraction and packet inspection.

AI in Intrusion Detection: Supervised learning using classification models (Decision Tree), model evaluation using metrics like detection rate and false positive rate.

Data Preprocessing: Packet filtering, normalization, and feature selection.

Real-time Detection Challenges: Emphasizes the importance of low latency and high accuracy.

Zero-Day Detection Strategy: AI-based adaptability to evolving attack vectors.

 Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy

Precision

Recall

Detection Rate

False Positive Rate

 Tools & Technologies
Python 3.11+

Pandas, scikit-learn, NumPy

Jupyter Notebook (optional, for testing)

Scapy / Pyshark (planned for real network simulation)

Mininet (optional for network simulation)

Future Enhancements
Integration with scapy for live packet sniffing and feature extraction.

GUI dashboard for visualization of alerts.

Extended model testing on zero-day attack datasets.

Model optimization using Random Forest or ensemble methods.

Checklist
 Dataset preprocessed and loaded

 Model trained and serialized

 Live detection simulated with test inputs

 Background research integrated in README and comments

 Project organized and documented

* Fix uninformative error message (:issue:`830`)
* Refactor ``canonicalize_version`` (:issue:`793`)
* Patch python_full_version unconditionally (:issue:`825`)
* Fix doc for ``canonicalize_version`` to mention ``strip_trailing_zero`` and a typo in a docstring (:issue:`801`)
* Fix typo in Version ``__str__`` (:issue:`817`)
* Support creating a ``SpecifierSet`` from an iterable of ``Specifier`` objects (:issue:`775`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 24.1
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Document ``markers.default_environment()`` (:issue:`753`).
* Add support for Python 3.13 (:issue:`783`).
* Modernise type annotations (:issue:`785`).
* Work around ``platform.python_version()`` returning non PEP 440 compliant version
  for non-tagged CPython builds (:issue:`802`).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 24.0

   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Do specifier matching correctly when the specifier contains an epoch number
  and has more components than the version (:issue:`683`)

  (:issue:`727`)
* BREAKING: Make optional ``metadata.Metadata`` attributes default to ``None`` (:issue:`733`)
* Fix errors when trying to access the ``description_content_type``, ``keywords``,
  and ``requires_python`` attributes on ``metadata.Metadata`` when those values
  have not been provided (:issue:`733`)
* Fix a bug preventing the use of the built in ``ExceptionGroup`` on versions of
  Python that support it (:issue:`725`)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 23.2
   ```
   ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

* Document calendar-based versioning scheme (:issue:`716`)
* Enforce that the entire marker string is parsed (:issue:`687`)
* Requirement parsing no longer automatically validates the URL (:issue:`120`)
* Canonicalize names for requirements comparison (:issue:`644`)
* Introduce ``metadata.Metadata`` (along with ``metadata.ExceptionGroup`` and ``metadata.InvalidMetadata``; :issue:`570`)
* Introduce the ``validate`` keyword parameter to ``utils.normalize_name()`` (:issue:`570`)
* Introduce ``utils.is_normalized_name()`` (:issue:`570`)

  raise ``InvalidSdistFilename`` and ``InvalidWheelFilename``, respectively,
  when the version component of the name is invalid
* Remove support for Python 3.7 (:issue:`783`)

* Parse raw metadata (:issue:`671`)
* Import underlying parser functions as an underscored variable (:issue:`663`)
* Improve error for local version label with unsupported operators (:issue:`675`)
* Add dedicated error for specifiers with incorrect `.*` suffix
* Replace spaces in platform names with underscores (:issue:`620`)
* Relax typing of ``_key`` on ``_BaseVersion`` (:issue:`669`)
* Handle prefix match with zeros at end of prefix correctly (:issue:`674`)

* Allow ``"extra"`` to be ``None`` in the marker environment (:issue:`650`)
* Refactor ``tags._generic_api`` to use ``EXT_SUFFIX`` (:issue:`607`)
* Correctly handle trailing whitespace on URL requirements (:issue:`642`)
* Fix typing for ``specifiers.BaseSpecifier.filter()`` (:issue:`643`)
* Use stable Python 3.11 in tests (:issue:`641`)
* Correctly handle non-normalised specifiers in requirements (:issue:`634`)

author: cho-m
body:
Related to https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/220708

Will be experimenting with various patches/inreplaces to help unbundle freeimage.

Only bundled dependencies are supported by upstream. Most of unbundling is already done by applying Debian patch (which is a similar patch carried by Fedora, Arch, Gentoo, etc). Went with Debian as we can also get a few CVE fixes.

---

The extra patches here include:
1. `imath-int64.patch` - Similar to https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/freeimage/blob/rawhide/f/freeimage-openexr3.patch but the minimal set needed. Debian doesn't have a patch for this. Mainly impacts macOS due to some _long_ vs _long long_.
2. `libtiff-warning.patch` - This is patch on top of Debian/Fedora's patched TIFF code. It looks like Fedora logic used in patch will trigger `libtiff`'s stderr and cause flooding of warning messages seen in `perpetualdiff`. For now, just disable warning output for the patched logic.
3. `macos.patch` is based on our `3.17.0.patch` though I changed install_name to VERLIBNAME so that linkage happens using versioned path matching the compatibility version. This matches Linux library SONAME and MacPorts https://github.com/macports/macports-ports/blob/master/graphics/freeimage/Portfile#L56
4. `debian-to-homebrew.patch` - a couple things in Debian patch don't work in Homebrew

---

Revamped the old patches for HEAD usage as it is difficult to carry an unbundle patch there.

In follow up, I may just remove HEAD as it bundled libs don't build on macOS 15.4. On Linux, it builds but something is wrong with bundled `libtiff`

author: vpaesi
body:
Este _pull request_ introduz um conjunto significativo de mudanças, com foco na adição da configuração do Jest para testes, no aprimoramento da aplicação com componentes reutilizáveis e na melhoria do roteamento e da autenticação. Abaixo está um resumo das alterações mais importantes:

### Configuração de Testes
Adicionada a configuração do Jest em jest.config.ts para habilitar suporte a TypeScript e ESM, configurar jsdom como ambiente de testes e definir a coleta de cobertura.

Criado o arquivo jest.setup.ts para incluir @testing-library/jest-dom e simular a API fetch para testes.

Atualizado o package.json para incluir dependências do Jest e da Testing Library, além de adicionar um script test para execução dos testes.

### Roteamento e Autenticação
Aprimorado o arquivo src/App.tsx com a introdução do componente PrivateRoute para proteger rotas, adicionar verificações de autenticação e integrar o react-toastify para notificações.

Atualizado o componente src/components/Header.tsx para ajustar dinamicamente os links de navegação com base no estado de autenticação e adicionar um botão de logout.

### Componentes Reutilizáveis
Adicionados os componentes reutilizáveis: Button, Alert, Card, Form, InputField, ImageUpload, LoadingScreen e LoadingSpinner, todos com props personalizáveis para maior flexibilidade. [[1]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[2]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[3]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[4]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[5]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[6]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[7]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1) [[8]](https://github.com/vpaesi/fala-cidadao/compare/develop?expand=1)

### Formulários e Validação
Criado o formulário DadosPessoaisForm para lidar com a entrada de dados pessoais, com validações para campos como CPF e número de telefone.

Desenvolvido o EnderecoForm para gerenciamento da entrada de dados de endereço, incluindo busca dinâmica de cidades com base no estado selecionado e formatação de CEP.

Essas alterações, em conjunto, aprimoram a infraestrutura de testes da aplicação, melhoram a experiência do usuário com componentes reutilizáveis e fortalecem os mecanismos de roteamento e autenticação.

This pull request introduces several changes to enhance the `Courses` API functionality, including adding an `update` endpoint, improving authorization, and enhancing test coverage. The most significant changes include the addition of the `update` action in the `CoursesController`, updates to role-based abilities, and the addition of comprehensive tests for the `CoursesController`.

### API Enhancements:
* Added an `update` action to `Api::V1::CoursesController`, enabling updates to course attributes. The action includes authorization checks and error handling for invalid inputs.
* Updated the `routes.rb` file to include the `update` endpoint for `courses`.
* Modified the `show` and `update` views to use a shared `_course` partial for rendering course attributes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5454265cd5f991f6f716ca159020a8d735d2c1208e322e3ccc8877a29c824320L3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f360a4d90ba13733568aceed40686ada7b8a794e31bd579548bfdf224cc51099R1-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1bdf0d23c40cc103a8c78daeb84a0b5ed3df6fa3d4cb271ad1d5b5539f97669cR1-R3)

### Authorization Improvements:
* Updated `StudentAbility` and `TeacherAbility` to define role-specific permissions for `Course` resources. Students can `read` courses, while teachers can `read` and `update` courses. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-892db3b96bb1099b2f75e76d77bd4efef06b1a5ccb820461926fc20307aeee0dL11-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-934a2a31d7c0ae1482f7599d5b6cd09b195f375ce669f68bda785fb3283270fcL11-R17)

### Test Coverage:
* Added a new spec file for `Api::V1::CoursesController`, covering `show` and `update` actions with tests for success, failure, and authorization scenarios.
* Enhanced the test setup in `rails_helper.rb` to include Devise helpers for controller tests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-053aa3ea46cb7c6a649e0d0fc592ce729b66e1d44be475516fd58857ba695862R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-053aa3ea46cb7c6a649e0d0fc592ce729b66e1d44be475516fd58857ba695862R37-R38)

### Minor Updates:
* Improved error messages for `RecordNotFound` in the `set_course` method of `CoursesController`.
* Updated the `db/seeds/courses.rb` file to modify course descriptions for consistency.

body:
## Summary

We have changed `PoissonLikelihood` into `poisson_likelihood,` which compiles very fast and takes less memory than before.

## Related To

- #454 

## Description

In this PR, we have explored the use **padded arrays** for data to make their shapes same. We padded the data, reference priors, and an extra mask array to remember the padded values. When we have the same shape arrays, we could apply the `jax.vmap` transformation to calculate the likelihood of a single event. This was exhausting resources, therefore we moved to `jax.lax.scan` and it is working like a charm. We are getting faster compilation times, good speed, and low memory consumption.

## Additional Notes (Optional)

#525 contains partial changes and was merged accidentally.

author: koyopro
body:
This pull request introduces encryption for the payload of JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) using AES-CBC, enhances error handling, and updates dependencies to support the new functionality. The most important changes include adding the `crypto-js` library, modifying the `CookieStorage` class to encrypt and decrypt JWT payloads, and adding tests to validate the encryption and decryption process.

This closes #3 

### Encryption and Decryption of JWT Payloads:
* Updated the `restore` method in the `CookieStorage` class to decrypt JWT payloads using AES-CBC when the payload is a string. Added logic to handle JSON parsing errors gracefully. (`src/storage.ts`, [src/storage.tsL55-R81](diffhunk://#diff-10d5d48c419530b01c345d22a42140d1a726097de84b7525de74f8d5f6fbccc7L55-R81))
* Modified the `save` method in the `CookieStorage` class to encrypt the payload using AES-CBC before signing it with the JWT. Added comments explaining the choice of AES-CBC and its reliance on the JWT signature for tamper resistance. (`src/storage.ts`, [src/storage.tsL55-R81](diffhunk://#diff-10d5d48c419530b01c345d22a42140d1a726097de84b7525de74f8d5f6fbccc7L55-R81))

### Dependency Updates:
* Added `crypto-js` and its TypeScript types as dependencies in `package.json` to enable AES encryption and decryption. (`package.json`, [package.jsonR34-R36](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R34-R36))

### Test Enhancements:
* Added a new test case to verify that the JWT payload is encrypted and cannot be parsed as plaintext JSON. (`tests/index.test.ts`, [tests/index.test.tsR78-R93](diffhunk://#diff-cece62ae24396a5d51e8f2a2cb3abba900652084488023f4de9669eaaf6f81e8R78-R93))
* Introduced a test case to validate the decryption and verification of JWTs, ensuring the correct restoration of session data. (`tests/index.test.ts`, [tests/index.test.tsR78-R93](diffhunk://#diff-cece62ae24396a5d51e8f2a2cb3abba900652084488023f4de9669eaaf6f81e8R78-R93))

author: arslan8
body:
# Contributing to CSrankings

Thanks for contributing to CSrankings! Please read and indicate you agree with **all** these guidelines to getting your pull request accepted. Note that pull requests may take some time to get merged (please don't contact us for at least three months for updates, unless you are a sponsor - see below).

**If you find CSrankings useful, [please consider becoming a sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/csrankings).**

**NOTE:** IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THE STEPS BELOW, YOUR PULL REQUEST WILL BE SUMMARILY REJECTED.
You must read and check **all** the boxes below by filling them in with an X or your PR will be rejected.

**The Basics**

- [ ] All pull requests and issues must come from non-anonymous accounts. Make sure your GitHub profile contains your full name.

- [ ] Use a reasonable title that explains what the PR corresponds to (as in, not "Update csrankings-x.csv").

- [ ] Combine multiple updates to a single institution into a **single PR.**

- [ ] Only submit one pull request per institution.

- [ ] Do not modify any files except `csrankings-[a-z].csv` or (if needed) `country-info.csv` and `old/industry.csv` (see below).

- [ ] Do not use Excel to edit any .csv files; Excel incorrectly tries to
convert some Google Scholar entries to formulas, corrupting the
database. Use the GitHub user interface or a text editor like emacs or NotePad instead.

- [ ] Insert new faculty **in alphabetical order** (not at the end) in the appropriate `csrankings-[a-z].csv` files. **Do not modify `csrankings.csv`, which is auto-generated.**

- [ ] Check to make sure that you have no spaces after commas, or any missing fields.

- [ ] Check to make sure the home page is correct.

- [ ] Make sure the Google Scholar IDs are just the alphanumeric identifier (not a URL or with `&hl=en`).

- [ ] Check to make sure the name corresponds to the DBLP entry (look it up at http://dblp.org).

- [ ] If a faculty member is not in a CS department or similar, include a comment explaining how they meet the inclusion criteria (see below).

**Inclusion criteria**

- [ ] Make sure that any faculty you add meet the inclusion
criteria. Eligible faculty include only full-time, tenure-track research
faculty members on a given campus who can *solely* advise PhD students in
Computer Science. Faculty not in a CS department or similar who can
advise PhD students in CS can be included regardless of their home
department. **Provide justification, pointing to specific home pages
showing how faculty not in a CS department meet the inclusion criteria,
e.g. showing a courtesy appointment in CS.** Faculty must also have a 75%+ time appointment (check
`old/industry.csv` for faculty who are now more than 25% in industry).

**Updating an affiliation or home page**

- [ ] Update affiliations, home pages, and Google Scholar entries by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv`. For the Google Scholar entry, just use the alphanumeric identifier in the middle of the URL. If none is there, put `NOSCHOLARPAGE`.

**Adding one or more faculty members (including an entire department)**

- [ ] If the department is not yet listed in CSrankings, the entire CS faculty needs to be added (not just one faculty member).

- [ ] Enter each faculty member's [DBLP](http://dblp.org) name, home page, and Google Scholar entry (just the alphanumeric identifier, not the whole URL) by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv` (**the letters correspond to the first letter of the faculty members' names**); include disambiguation suffixes like `0001` as needed. If the faculty entry is currently ambiguous, please do not include them. Send mail to the DBLP maintainers (dblp@dagstuhl.de) with a few publications by a particular faculty member; also, open an issue so that when the DBLP database is updated, that faculty member's information can be added.

- [ ] If DBLP has multiple entries for this person, *all of them need to be listed*. Do not update `dblp-aliases.csv`.

- [ ] If the institution you are adding is not in the US,
update `country-info.csv` and add *all* of the faculty in the CS department.

**(Advanced) Quick contribution via a shallow clone** 

We recommend that you use the GitHub web user interface to make changes. However, it may be more convenient
to clone the repository for larger-scale changes.

However, a full clone of the CSrankings repository is almost 2GB.  To
contribute a change without creating a full local clone of the
CSrankings repo, you can perform a _shallow clone_.  To do so, follow these
steps:

1. Fork the CSrankings repo.  If you have an existing fork, but it is not up to date with the main repository, this technique may not work.  If necessary, delete and re-create your fork to get it up to date.  (Do **not** delete your existing fork if it has unmerged changes you want to preserve!)

1. Do a shallow clone of your fork: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yourusername/CSrankings`.  This will only download the most recent commit, not the full git history.

1. Make your changes on a branch, push them to your clone, and create a pull request on GitHub as usual.

If you want to make another contribution and some time has passed, perform these steps again, creating a fresh fork and shallow clone.

author: childofdreams
body:
Currently, the MD queue system expects every datagram to be added to it sequentially. This causes issues when a datagram being processed creates more datagrams; these new datagrams always get appended to the end of the queue, which can cause some datagrams to ultimately finish their process later than those that entered later.

Since some games using OtpGo expect the packet order to be consistent, the MD queue is now a map of `QueueEntry` slices, and a `RouteDatagramEarly` function was added to append a datagram to the current QueueEntry slice. 

For now, this early routing is used for field updates (+ DB datagrams) and datagrams relevant to DO generation; it is possible that other datagram routing calls will need to update to use this later.

This PR standardizes the WLAN Pi OS version format to use hyphens (-) for separating version components, replacing the previous mix of underscores (_) and tildes (~). This brings more consistency to our versioning schema.

<!-- *Pick at least one.* -->

* [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes something)

<!-- *Please describe the purpose of this change, the problem it solves, and why the change is necessary. Including code snippets or links to related documentation when applicable will assist approval.* -->

- Replace format `YYYY.MM.DD_rc.N` with `YYYY.MM.DD-rc.N` for release candidates
- Replace format `YYYY.MM.DD~dev.N` with `YYYY.MM.DD-dev.N` for development builds

body: Fixes #109 **What was changed:** Right now, only the threshold is sent to the backend when the submit button is presssed in the ResearcherToolbar component. This PR adds support for the movingAverageFactor variable as well. Tests to verify the correct functionality of this feature were added as well. **Why was this changed:** In order for the researcher to change the MAF and threshold parameters. **How was it changed:** Adding support for MAF into the sendThreshold function required changing the format from expecting only the threshold to any object. In order to reduce redundancy and websocket payloads, flags were set to watch for threshold and MAF updates, so that when the submit button is pressed, only updated parameters would be sent to the backend. This was done by creating an empty object and adding whichever variables were flagged as changed from the previous button press. A few tests were added to make sure only the updated variables were added to the payload, and the existing test, which verified the correct values sent, were expanded to test MAF in addition to threshold values.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/pwnlaboratory/jetpack/security/code-scanning/55](https://github.com/pwnlaboratory/jetpack/security/code-scanning/55)

To fix the SSRF vulnerability, we need to validate and sanitize the user-controlled `req.url` before using it to construct the `upstreamUrl`. Specifically:
1. Ensure that the `req.url` does not contain malicious path traversal sequences (e.g., `../`) or unexpected query parameters.
2. Use a whitelist approach to allow only specific paths or patterns that are known to be safe.
3. Reject or sanitize any input that does not conform to the expected format.

The fix involves:
- Parsing the `req.url` using the `URL` class to extract and validate the pathname.
- Ensuring the pathname does not contain any path traversal sequences or invalid characters.
- Constructing the `upstreamUrl` using the sanitized pathname.

author: dalevyy
body:
# Summary
This PR closes #57 and integrates the ability for PRISM users to identify students that are using blacklisted keywords inside their code submissions.

# Description
This script is designed to track which students were found using keywords and/or libraries that they weren't supposed to. This will be determined by the professor during either the creation of the assignment or at a later point after the assignment has been due. By @ortegj8 request, this script will do a bulk analysis for all sections corresponding to a single assignment.

The first portion of the analysis will be for headers. This will be done manually since `std` C++ header files will contain their own headers, and we want to avoid false positives. The second portion of the analysis is the actual usage of keywords or other library specific methods. In this case, I found the `libclang` package that will automatically parse and generate the C++ AST for us. I generate the AST and then do a recursive visit on the tree, and I check if the current node's text field matches any of the keywords specified by the user. If we do find a match, we then make sure it's not a variable declaration or a name expression to ensure the user didn't use the keyword as an identifier before we add its usage to the errors list.

Once all analysis has been done for a single student, then we will add the student's data into the json file if there were any instances of the banned keyword usage. We repeat this process until all students have been checked, and then the json file is ready to be returned to the front end.

# Documentation
New Packages/Files:
1. `code_analysis`: This is a new package that will store all scripts relating to student code analysis in PRISM.
2. `code_analysis/keyword_detection`: Inside the `code_analysis` package, I have created a subpackage that will store the script and files needed to do the check for blacklisted keywords.
3. `keywordAnalysis.py`: This is the main script for this PR. This script should be executed as any other Python script, and you should specify the file name containing the banned keywords. This file should be stored in the `keyword_detection` subpackage. In the future, we will probably change the input method to directly interface with the database instead.

Input File Format: 
- Title: `as<assignmentNum>_banned_words.txt`
- Data: Each line should be a separate keyword/library that the user wants to check for
- Example Image:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3988e4d7-4285-4ab0-8223-e5b24880bfc8)

Output File Format:
- Title: `<assignmentNum>_found.json`
- Data: Each json file will have all the sections listed for each assignment. Each section will contain a list of students that were found to have banned keywords in their files. This will include a list of the header files that they shouldn't have followed by the usage of each keyword and the line number the keyword was used on.
- Example Image:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3912d88a-b079-42a5-825d-98e98859a958)


# Unit Tests
**No Tests.**

I have not written unit tests for this file yet since there isn't much error checking to be done (since at this point, the students file should exist based on the scripts I wrote for PRs #24 and #32). I will consider doing unit tests in the future if the team would like me to include them.

# PR Reviews
I would like @ortegj8 , @eliJerald , and/or @stevenfojas670 to take a look at this PR and, at the bare minimum, look at how the input/output data should be formatted. However, anyone may review this PR 😄

<!-- If you are new to the Delta-V repository, please read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/DeltaV-Station/Delta-v/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) -->

## About the PR
If you move out of range with a health analyzer and then back into range, it will set your health analyzer window back to active! No more re-scanning the same patient!

## Why / Balance
God, its annoying to have to rescan a patient if you have to run to the chem locker to make sure they havent been treated by someone else, or if you have to move two feet away during surgery to pick up a body part that someone brought in. This is a QoL fix, pure and simple.

## Technical details
When one moves out of the scanning range, the scanned entities are no longer set to `null`. Instead, it will keep checking the range in the Update loop and once they are back within range, it will send an update back to the analyzer. Since setting the  scanner to inactive requires you to send the whole payload of health information (found in `Content.Shared\MedicalScanner\HealthAnalyzerScannedUserMessage.cs`), we also have to save the health analyzer state so that we only send the inactivation once, thus I added `IsAnalyzerActive` to the `HealthAnalyzerComponent` that tracks the last state of the health analyzer.

Also fixed the size of the Out of Range sprite to be more consistent with the shitmed sprites found in the analyzer window. It will no longer resize that image if you go out (or back into) range.
